distinguishing_features: Pressure-energized squeeze-film fluid barrier driven by line pressure into seat roughness valleys, rather than a solid gasket, hardened material, or altered seat geometry
Sealing mechanism closes the Fickian permeation path physically via a hydrogen-impermeable liquid film rather than by bulk toughness or reduced driving force
Relaxes local static stress intensity factor KI at the seat by converting static contact pressure into a pressure-proportional dynamic film pressure
Passive, self-scaling barrier whose strength tracks line pressure (P_film ≈ P_line) rather than a fixed-limit static clamp
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Preventing hydrogen-emitted seat leakage by physically blocking micro-porosity permeation paths and reducing stress-concentration-driven crack initiation at the valve seat under high-pressure hydrogen service.
parsed.viable_reason: The scheme requires a stable hydrogen-impermeable low-viscosity fluid film at 70 MPa across a 5 µm gap, but no fluid is shown to remain immiscible, non-permeating, and non-exuding under such conditions, and the claim that P_interface>P_line gives zero permeation driving force is physically incoherent, making it unvalidated as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: The pressure-energized squeeze-film liquid barrier concept is not an obvious routine extension of any cited art (dosing, ΔP inference, or current normalization), so the distinguishing mechanism itself would not be an obvious step, though the feasibility fails.
